newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat ends lower on beneficial rainfall.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat ends lower on beneficial rainfall.

text.p: MGE spring wheat futures settled sharply lower and new crop September fell to its lowest price in three months after much-needed rains fell in dry growing areas of North Dakota, traders said.
MGE spring wheat had gained relative to KCBT and CBOT wheat in recent weeks on concern over the lack of moisture in North Dakota.

"Good rains over the weekend collapsed things and we hit sell stops on the way down," a MGE trader said. "There are also some forecasts for rains later this week, so that (provided additional pressure)," a MGE trader said.
MGE spring wheat settled 12-1/2 to 15-1/4 cents per bushel lower. New crop September lost 15-1/4 cents to close at $3.74-1/2, its lowest close since March 7, when it ended at $3.72-3/4.
Featured players included Cargill Investor Services, which sold 1.7 million Sept bushels. Benson-Quinn sold 1.3 million July and 700,000 Sept, traders said.
